newsitem.title: USA: Bowles to testify before Whitewater grand jury.
newsitem.headline: Bowles to testify before Whitewater grand jury.

text.p: White House chief of staff Erskine Bowles was scheduled to testify Tuesday before a grand jury investigating the Whitewater affair in Little Rock, Arkansas, a White House official said.

"He is testifying before the grand jury in Arkansas," said Bowles aide Beverly Barnes. Barnes said she did know what subjects would come up, nor when the testimony would begin or end, but she said Bowles was expected back at the White House Wednesday.

Bowles received a subpoena from the grand jury demanding both documents and testimony on April 4, three days after the White House disclosed that he and former chief of staff Thomas "Mack" McLarty, had sought to help Webster Hubbell find work after he resigned from a top post at the Justice Department.

Hubbell, once a close friend of President Bill Clinton and a law partner of his wife, Hillary Rodham Clinton, resigned as associate attorney general amid controversy over his work as a private citizen and went to jail in 1995 after he pleaded guilty to fraudulent billing of clients at the Rose Law Firm in Little Rock before he joined the Clinton administration.
Barnes said she did not know how long Bowles testimony in Little Rock would last, but said: "We expect him in the office tomorrow (on Wednesday)."

The White House has rejected suggestions that the effort to help Hubbell find work constituted "hush money" to secure his silence about Whitewater, a failed Arkansas land deal that Clinton, his wife and some of their friends invested in when he was governor of the state.
